entities.name: Glaucias of Macedon
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Glaucias of Macedon was a prominent military officer in the Macedonian army during the turbulent post-Alexandrian era, active in the late 4th century BCE. While his birth date remains unrecorded, his life culminated around 400 BCE, placing him squarely within the Wars of the Diadochi, a period of intense power struggles following Alexander the Great's death. His historical significance stems from his participation in pivotal campaigns under Alexander and, more controversially, his alleged role in the elimination of the Argead royal line, specifically the young king Alexander IV and his mother Roxana. His actions, if confirmed, directly contributed to the consolidation of Cassander's power and the eventual fragmentation of Alexander's vast empire into independent Hellenistic kingdoms.

Initially serving with distinction, Glaucias is recorded as an officer of the elite Companion cavalry, the heavy cavalry arm of the Macedonian army, at the decisive Battle of Gaugamela in 331 BCE. This engagement saw Alexander the Great utterly defeat Darius III of Persia, paving the way for the conquest of the Achaemenid Empire. After Alexander's death in 323 BCE, Glaucias's career took a darker turn. Historical accounts, notably those of Diodorus Siculus, implicate him as the agent of Cassander, one of Alexander's generals vying for control, in the murders of Alexander IV and Roxana. These assassinations, carried out in the citadel of Amphipolis around 310 BCE, were a calculated act to eliminate the legitimate heirs to Alexander's throne, thereby clearing Cassander's path to kingship over Macedon.
